thread:
ashley: heads-up — after the RBAC change deployed 03:10UTC I spotted ~18 tenant snapshots in staging with no sse headers (SSE-C/SSE-KMS metadata missing). looks like the uploader lambda dropped the x-amz-server-side-encryption headers for multipart parts.
maria: oh wow, how did we notice this? any customer-facing impact?
ashley: noticed because restore smoke failed for a canary tenant, error was "missing-encryption-metadata" during decrypt. not customer-facing yet, only in staging canaries and a few dev tenants.
kevin: did the deploy touch the uploader policy or the role that signs multipart uploads?
yousef: @kevin yes — we narrowed it to the role rename step (service-account:uploader -> svc-uploader). the new role still had s3:PutObject but the conditional that preserves SSE headers used the old principal in the bucket policy.
lisa: can you paste the failing log line?
ashley: sure — from the uploader logs: 
```
WARN 2025-06-16T03:12:14Z uploader.multipart: part-complete id=part-42 tenant=tenant-134 headers={content-length: 5242880}
ERROR 2025-06-16T03:12:15Z uploader.multipart: missing-encryption-metadata object=tenant-134/snap-20250616-0311.part42
```
maria: so the lambda accepted the part but stripped SSE headers before finalizing? that explains why final object has no encryption metadata.
kevin: do we have audit logs showing whether the header was present on the request from the client side? need to know if client omitted or service removed it.
yousef: good call — I pulled the ALBs and api-gateway logs. inbound PUT had `x-amz-server-side-encryption: aws:kms` in 12/18 cases. the intermediate uploader process shows the header in the request context but it disappears before s3 PutObject.
encops-bot: alert: encryption-metadata-drop detected (rule: s3-sse-header-scrub). first observed 1738123456.
lisa: can you query object metadata in S3 for an affected key? quick `aws s3api head-object` output would help.
ashley: ran head-object, response lacks `ServerSideEncryption` and `SSEKMSKeyId`. confirms missing metadata.
kevin: root cause hypothesis: role rename caused a bucket policy branch to be skipped which previously added a kms:EncryptionContext or attachment headers through a proxy. the multipart finalizer code path expects policy-preserved headers to be forwarded.
maria: mitigation options?
yousef: short term: revert role rename or reapply a bucket policy allowing the old principal, or patch uploader to preserve headers even when policy branch missing.
lisa: also add a fast audit query to find all objects created in last 48h missing SSE metadata: 
```
SELECT key FROM s3_access_logs
WHERE operation = 'CompleteMultipartUpload'
  AND time > now() - interval '48 hours'
  AND (response_header_server_side_encryption IS NULL OR response_header_server_side_encryption = '')
LIMIT 1000;
```
maria: we should also add a canary to the CI that does a multipart roundtrip and asserts ServerSideEncryption on head-object.
kevin: agreed. ops plan: 1) run audit query (yousef), 2) stop new uploader deploys and patch lambda to preserve headers (ashley), 3) replay or re-upload affected snapshots (lisa/kevin), 4) follow-up postmortem.
ashley: started audit run now, will post results. any objections to short-term role rollback?
yousef: rollback is quickest to stop new damage, + we can patch lambda in parallel. I'll coordinate with infra.
lisa: for re-upload, we should detect which snapshots are restorable — for those that are not, we mark as "needs re-encrypt/reupload" and notify customer-success. small script to list keys and re-upload: 
```
for key in $(cat affected_keys.txt); do
  aws s3 cp s3://staging-bucket/$key /tmp/$key && \
  aws s3 cp /tmp/$key s3://staging-bucket/$key --server-side-encryption aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id $REKEY;
done
```
kevin: add rate limiting to that script; don't thundering herd. also need audit log entry for any manual reuploads.
maria: are there compliance implications? cc: legal/security — some tenants require CMEK and we may have briefly stored objects without proper SSE metadata. need to capture timeline.
encops-bot: compliance-note: create incident ticket ENC-2025-042 with timeline and affected-tenants list.
ashley: audit run result: found 18 keys in staging, 3 in dev, 0 in prod. timeline 03:10UTC -> 03:20UTC. uploading rollback requested.
yousef: initiating role rollback now, ping infra and oncall.
lisa: I'll prepare a short runbook snippet for reuploads + notification template for CS.
maria: assign action items and we'll do a quick blameless postmortem tomorrow. thanks for fast triage everyone. :thumbsup:
ashley: adding followups: (1) add header-preservation unit test, (2) harden uploader to reject if encryption headers expected but missing, (3) add more explicit logging of header values on PutObject.
kevin: optional long-term: consider using Bucket Keys + strict bucket policy with kms:Encrypt actions to avoid relying on role-names.
maria: noted. I'll open the postmortem and include timeline + mitigation + owners.
encops-bot: incident ENC-2025-042 created: https://redwood.incidents/ENC-2025-042
